tools.name: create_account
tools.description: Sign the person up with their email. Returns an API key to put in the MCP config (Authorization: Bearer <key>). The person gets an email to verify; the profile goes live after that. Works without a key.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: The person's own profile, status (live / incomplete / waiting for email verification), missing fields, credit balance, and private agent_brief. Call this first.

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Set any profile fields; only the fields you pass change. Required to go live: name, birthdate, gender, looking_for, city, bio. Optional details: height_cm, occupation, employer, education, school, income, hometown, languages, pronouns, orientation, ethnicity, religion, politics, drinking, smoking, c

tools.name: add_photo
tools.description: Add a photo of your person to their profile (max 6). Pass either a public https image url or base64 image data (JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB). The image is copied into Crushy's storage. Only use photos your person gave you.

tools.name: remove_photo
tools.description: Remove a photo by its url (from get_me). To reorder photos, call update_profile with the photos list in the new order.

tools.name: discover
tools.description: Search for new, mutually compatible people. Translate your person's request into filters (exact) and query (free text), e.g. "blonde, about 5'6, dimples, doesn't smoke, six figures" -> filters {hair_color:["blonde"], features:["dimples"], smoking:["never"], income:["100k_150k","150k_250k","250k_plus

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Re-read a profile you already received from discover, or a match. Free.

tools.name: swipe
tools.description: Like or pass on a profile you've seen (from discover, likes_received or history). Decisions can always be changed: swipe again. If they already liked your person, a like makes a match and returns match_id. Passing on someone you're matched with unmatches; liking them again re-opens the match if they

tools.name: get_updates
tools.description: Everything new since your last check, in one call: new matches (with why they liked your person) and new messages from matches. Pass the cursor from the previous call; omit it the first time (covers the last 7 days). Use this instead of polling list_matches and read_messages.

tools.name: list_matches
tools.description: All active matches with the other person's profile, why each side liked the other, the last message and unread count.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Messages in a match, oldest first. Pass after_id to get only newer ones. Marks them read.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message in a match. It is labeled as sent by an agent. The people can also chat on the website.

tools.name: block
tools.description: Block someone: ends any match and hides both people from each other until your person unblocks them (unblock). Pass profile_id or match_id. Add a reason to also report them for review (harassment, fake profile, underage, scam). To just end a match, use unmatch instead.

tools.name: likes_received
tools.description: People who liked your person and aren't matched with them yet, newest first, as full profiles. Like one back with swipe to match instantly. 1 credit the first time you see each person (seen_before:true is free). Their note stays hidden until you match. include_decided:true also lists people you alre

tools.name: unmatch
tools.description: End a match. Nobody is blocked: liking them again later re-opens the match (conversation kept) if they still like your person. Use block instead to hide someone for good.

tools.name: unblock
tools.description: Lift a block your person placed (find them with history decision:"blocked"). They can appear in searches again; a previous match is not restored automatically, but liking them again re-opens it if they still like your person.

tools.name: history
tools.description: Everyone your agent has already seen, newest first, with the decision (like / pass / undecided), your note, and match_id if matched. decision:"blocked" lists people your person blocked (unblock to reverse). Filter by decision, e.g. undecided to finish reviewing, or pass to reconsider; to change a de

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Report a problem or a gap to the Crushy team: results that didn't fit the request, a search you couldn't express with the filters, a confusing error, a missing feature, or a bug. Include what your person asked for in context. Free; read by humans and used to improve search.

tools.name: delete_account
tools.description: Permanently delete your person's account: profile, photos, matches, messages and remaining credits. Cannot be undone. Only when your person explicitly asks; pass confirm:"DELETE". To just hide the profile for a while, use update_profile({paused:true}) instead.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description: Get a Stripe payment link for a prepaid credit pack. Give the link to your person; credits arrive after payment. Packs: starter = 200 credits for $10, plus = 500 credits for $20, max = 1500 credits for $50 (USD, plus any tax due where your person lives, added at checkout).

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_account" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "discover" is 1525 chars, far longer than this server's median (243). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "discover" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "send_feedback" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_me, remove_photo, get_updates, list_matches, read_messages · Private data: create_account, get_me · Public sink: create_account, get_me, send_message, send_feedback · Destructive: remove_photo, delete_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_me, remove_photo, get_updates, list_matches, read_messages · Private data: create_account, get_me · Public sink: create_account, get_me, send_message, send_feedback · Destructive: remove_photo, delete_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
